scores.notes: The head forming grin-first, the flamingo set down and Alice beginning to speak fall within one or two minutes of the same paragraph; the order of putting the flamingo down is not a different instant.
The swamp adder is selected, but Watson 'saw nothing' at this instant; selecting it invites a drawn snake the moment does not show.
An anonymous runner shedding a weight before tiers of onlookers is the verse's own image, not the writer or a named listener placed in a scene; no fault the question names.
The plan shows the men rising in the centre and already falling at the edges, two instants at once, which the question names directly.
The instruction's content is Moses anointing Aaron, and Moses is the one told to do it; unlike a law verse whose recipients are drawn as the subject, the drawn act is the verse's subject.
The King's pointing and the Queen's throw are consecutive lines of one exchange inside the moment and can share a frame; no other event or place is drawn.
Watson is the narrator; leaving him out as the viewpoint is allowed, and the text's visible subjects (Holmes on his knees with the lantern and lens, Merryweather on the crate) are all there.
A title verse with no scene; the plan asks for no writing, and both scorers found no fault. The risk of carved inscriptions is a rendering matter for the image tier.
Naomi speaks at home after Ruth returns; the plan stands Ruth with her basket in the field Naomi's words describe, with the reapers working: the listener placed in the scene of the words.
Ezekiel is already in the valley among the bones (37:1-2) when told to prophesy; the plan holds the instant before any movement, which is this verse's place and moment.
God speaks to Hosea (1:6); his presence as light and cloud seen from Hosea's house is the speech setting in the form the depiction rules allow, not a figure enacting the promise.
21:1 names only the new heaven, the new earth and the absent sea; God is selected as cast, with glory 'pouring down', though he enters the vision only from 21:3.

'We were all hastening' does not single out Bradstreet as a clearly shown subject, and the station-master is part of the moment's text; the plan is still flawed for its deep-night setting, which both scorers name.
Eliphaz's simile about the wicked man is staged on Job's ash heap, so the listener's place becomes the scene of the speaker's words; the speech's moment is not swapped for a different event.
The moment and place are right (John before the spring of the water of life); the glass sea and palm-bearers are added elements from other visions, recorded in the notes, not a different instant.
